questions.question:
**Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

At seven began the education that was to making the young boy a citizen and a soldier.

options.text: boy a citizen and a soldier
that was to making the young

questions.solution:
The erroneous part is** 'that was to making the young'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'that was to make the young' **should be used instead of** 'that was to making the young'.**
 
• We know that the base form of the verb is used after '**to**' **infinitive**.
 
 
• *Example: I decided **to go **home as soon as possible.*
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *At seven began the education that was to make the young boy a citizen and a soldier.*

• The most appropriate determiner for the given blank is '**these**'.

• Here, **'Many an old story was retold' **should be used instead of **'Many an old story were retold'.**
 
• According to the rules of **subject-verb agreement,** we know that after** 'Many a/an' **the base form of the **verb** and **singular** **noun** should be used.
 
 
• *Example: **Many a man has **tried but few men have succeeded. *
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is** Option 1.**

 

**​Correct Sentence:__** ***Many an old story was retold**, and an ancient conundrum repeated.*

• यदि 'Many a/an' के बाद वाक्य में संज्ञा का उपयोग होता है, तो वह संज्ञा एकवचन में होती है, और क्रिया भी एकवचन होती है। इसलिए, "Many an old story were retold" (बहुत सी पुरानी कहानियाँ फिर से कही गईं) की जगह "Many an old story was retold" (बहुत सी पुरानी कहानी फिर से कही गई) सही होगा।

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

Frank has being making / the rounds, advancing a theory / that I believe is not without merit.

options.text: that I believe is not without merit

questions.solution:
The erroneous part is '**Frank has being making**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, '**Frank has been making**' should be used instead of '**Frank has being making**'.
 
• The **perfect tenses **(past, present, and future) are formed with a form of 'have' and the past participle form of the main verb (had finished, has visited, have returned) for the **active voice.**
 
• The given sentence is in the** passive voice.**
 
• To use the** passive voice**, the word been is placed between the two (had been finished, has been visited, have been returned). 
 
 
• *Example: The reports** have been written.***
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** ***Frank has been making** the rounds, advancing a theory that I believe is not without merit.*
